name: Niger

nso.name: Institut National de la Statistique (INS Niger)

latest_census.notes: 4e Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat (RGP/H 2012), enumerated December 2012 (17.1M); definitive results and thematic reports 2014-2016. Ethnicity: recalled with good confidence -- the packet's national row (Hausa 53.1, Zarma/Songhai 21.2, Tuareg 11.0, Fulani 6.5; with Kanuri 5.9, Gourmantché 0.8, Arab 0.4, Toubou 0.4) is the RGP/H 2012 'ethnie' distribution published by INS and carried by the Factbook. Religion: recalled at medium confidence -- the 2012 questionnaire had a religion item (musulman / chrétien / animiste / autre / sans religion) and the ~99% Muslim figure is quoted from it; the packet's national religion row (95.5 / 4.1 / 0.3) is a non-census estimate. Language: null (I cannot recall whether 2012 asked 'langue parlée'). A 5th RGPH was scheduled for around 2022-2024; I do not know it to have been enumerated.

already_in_map: admin1 3/6 religion and ethnicity from Afrobarometer Round 9 (survey). The survey carries Niger's 8 regions (Agadez, Diffa, Dosso, Maradi, Tahoua, Tillabéri, Zinder, Niamey), but the boundary's admin1 layer draws only 6 shapes with merged labels 'Tahoua/Agadez' and 'Zinder/Diffa' and a misspelt 'Dossa', so only Maradi, Niamey and Tillaberi joined. That admin1 layer matches nothing Niger publishes (INS tabulates by 8 regions and 63 departments): a merged shape can only be filled by summing two regions' counts, which a survey's shares cannot do and a census's counts can. The admin2 layer (67) looks like the departments (Aguié, Arlit, Gothèye, Kantché, Madarounfa, Mirriah, Tibiri are departments; 63 departments + Niamey's 5 arrondissements = 68), so department-level census tables would join there.

subnational_sources.title: RGP/H 2012 -- Rapport d'analyse thématique 'État et structure de la population' (and/or 'Caractéristiques socioculturelles'): population by ethnie and by religion, by region
subnational_sources.matches_boundary_level: admin1 only partly: fills Dosso, Maradi, Niamey, Tillabéri directly; 'Tahoua/Agadez' and 'Zinder/Diffa' need two regions' counts summed (legitimate for a census count, not for the survey's shares)
subnational_sources.evidence: Recalled: the national ethnie shares are published by INS from this census, so a tabulation exists; the region breakdown is recalled from the thematic-report series, not verified.

subnational_sources.title: RGP/H 2012 -- Monographies régionales (one per region, 8): department-level tables
subnational_sources.evidence: Recalled series; whether the monographs tabulate ethnie/religion by department is unverified.

secondary_routes.hdx: Not recorded in the repo's USCB enumeration; OCHA COD admin boundaries for Niger (8 regions / departments) would be the fix for the merged admin1 layer -- the runner searches HDX itself.
secondary_routes.other: INS Niger also runs a NADA microdata catalogue (recalled) where the RGP/H 2012 questionnaire settles the religion and language columns.

tier_reason: A 2012 census count of ethnic group (certain) and religion (probable), recalled to be tabulated by region in INS's PDF thematic reports and possibly by department in the regional monographs; nothing known machine-readable except the ReNaLoc population gazetteer. The boundary's 6-shape admin1 layer is itself defective against Niger's 8 regions.
recommended_action: Crawl stat-niger.org for the RGP/H 2012 thematic reports and regional monographs; read ethnie and religion by region into admin1 (alias 'Dossa'->'Dosso'; fill 'Tahoua/Agadez' and 'Zinder/Diffa' by summing the two regions' counts, and say so in the record) and by department into admin2 if the monographs carry it. Flag the admin1 layer to the repo owner: six shapes for eight regions is a boundary defect worth replacing with an 8-region layer, after which the existing Afrobarometer rows for Agadez, Diffa, Dosso, Tahoua and Zinder would also join.
not_found: which 2012 volume carries ethnie/religion by region and whether any reaches department
whether the 2012 questionnaire had a language item
whether a 5th RGPH has been enumerated
any machine-readable INS publication of the two fields
summary: Niger's 2012 census asked ethnic group -- the packet's national shares are its distribution -- and, at medium confidence, religion, and INS published the results as PDF thematic reports by region and regional monographs that may reach department. The boundary is the harder problem: its admin1 layer draws six shapes for Niger's eight regions, two of them merged and one misspelt, so a region table joins only four shapes directly and the merged two only by summing census counts; the 67 admin2 shapes look like the departments and would join a department table cleanly. A census fill is PDF work and would replace the three Afrobarometer survey rows.
